Greek statues were often of lifelike ((++human alien)) bodies and were used to honour gods, ((++remember forget)) people and decorate spaces.

feedback.end: Ancient Greek statues were once painted in bright, vivid colours! Centuries of sun, rain and wind washed them away, leaving the bare stone we see today.

atoms.b: Ancient Greek vases were both ((++practical useless)) and decorative, used for storing food, ((++water electronics)) and oil.
They often featured detailed artwork showing scenes from ((++daily_life outer_space)) or myths, telling stories through painted ((++images billboards)).

trainers.instruction: Select the part of the vase that is being described.

atoms.a: In the center of the picture, you can see the hero Hercules fighting with a lion.
The goddess Athena watches the fight. She is wearing her iconic helmet and is holding a spear.
The figure behind Hercules is holding a club, sword and bow.
The lower part of the vase is decorated with patterns, and its base is black.
The upper part of the vase is also highly decorated. Like the base, the handles are black and were made separately from the body of the vase.

trainers.instruction: Interpret the picture on the vase. What do you see?

b: ++a scene from the myth of Hercules
an average scene from a market square in Athens
an important event during the Stone Age
